title: Rates and deals
goal: I can find a rate for 1 unit and use it to scale up. I can compare buys, and add rates when taps or machines work together.

learn.intro: A rate tells how much for 1 unit, such as litres in 1 minute. Find the amount for 1 unit first. Then multiply to scale up, or divide to find how long.

example.problem: A printer prints 90 pages in 6 minutes. How many pages does it print in 15 minutes? How many minutes does it need for 300 pages?
steps: Find the rate: 90 ÷ 6 = 15 pages in 1 minute.
example.answer: It prints 225 pages in 15 minutes. It needs 20 minutes for 300 pages.

howto.title: How to
steps: Multiply to scale up. Divide to find how long.
Check with the other way round.

facts.title: Buys and teams
lines: Better buy: find the cost of 1 item.
Taps working together: add the rates.
A leak: take its rate away.

try.text: A machine fills 24 bottles in 4 minutes. How many bottles does it fill in 11 minutes? {b}
try.explanation: 24 ÷ 4 = 6 bottles in 1 minute. In 11 minutes: 6 × 11 = 66 bottles.

items.text: A tap fills 18 litres in 3 minutes. Fill in the table. Write the missing numbers.
items.explanation: In 3 minutes: 18 litres. In 1 minute: 18 ÷ 3 = 6 litres. In 5 minutes: 5 × 6 = 30 litres. In 8 minutes: 8 × 6 = 48 litres.

items.text: 6 pens cost $4.20.
An oven bakes 36 rolls in 4 minutes.

parts.label: c
parts.text: It needs {b} minutes to bake 270 rolls.

items.explanation: (a) 36 ÷ 4 = 9 rolls a minute. (b) 25 × 9 = 225. (c) 270 ÷ 9 = 30 minutes.

items.text: Pack A has 5 pencils for $2.50. Pack B has 8 pencils for $3.60.

parts.label: c
parts.text: The better buy is   {circ:Pack A|Pack B}

items.explanation: (a) $2.50 ÷ 5 = $0.50. (b) $3.60 ÷ 8 = $0.45. (c) $0.45 is less than $0.50, so Pack B is the better buy.

items.text: Shop X sells 3 cans for $2.40. Shop Y sells 5 cans for $3.75. Mei needs 15 cans.

parts.label: c
parts.text: The cheaper shop is   {circ:Shop X|Shop Y}

items.explanation: 15 cans is 5 packs of 3 at X: 5 × $2.40 = $12.00. 15 cans is 3 packs of 5 at Y: 3 × $3.75 = $11.25. Shop Y is cheaper.

items.text: Tap A fills 14 litres a minute. Tap B fills 6 litres a minute. Both taps are on.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Together they fill {b} litres in 1 minute.

parts.label: b
parts.text: They need {b} minutes to fill a 200 litre tank.

items.explanation: (a) 14 + 6 = 20 litres a minute. (b) 200 ÷ 20 = 10 minutes.

items.text: A pump puts 25 litres a minute into a tank. A drain lets out 10 litres a minute. Both are on. In how many minutes is a 300 litre tank full? {b}
items.explanation: The tank gains 25 - 10 = 15 litres each minute. 300 ÷ 15 = 20 minutes.

items.text: Machine P folds 35 booklets each minute. Machine Q folds 25 booklets each minute. Together they fold one order of 1200 booklets. How many minutes does the order take? {b}
items.explanation: Together they fold 35 + 25 = 60 booklets a minute. 1200 ÷ 60 = 20 minutes.

items.text: A car park charges $3.00 for the first 2 hours. After that it charges $1.20 for each 15 minutes, and a part of 15 minutes counts as a whole one. Ravi parks for 3 hours 40 minutes. How much does he pay? $ {bw}
items.explanation: First 2 hours $3.00. Then 1 hour 40 minutes is 6 quarter hours and a part, so 7 lots: 7 × $1.20 = $8.40. Total $11.40.

items.text: A tank has 240 litres of water. A pump takes out 15 litres each minute.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The tank is empty after {b} minutes.

items.explanation: (a) 9 × 15 = 135 litres are taken out. 240 - 135 = 105 litres are left. (b) 240 ÷ 15 = 16 minutes.

items.text: A tap drips 4 ml of water every 10 seconds.
items.explanation: (a) 1 minute is 60 seconds, or 6 lots of 10 seconds. 6 × 4 = 24 ml. (b) 60 minutes: 60 × 24 = 1440 ml. (c) 1440 ÷ 1000 = 1.44 litres.

items.text: Circle True or False.

parts.label: a
parts.text: If 6 cans cost $3.60, then 12 cans cost $7.20.   {circ:True|False}

parts.label: b
parts.text: A larger pack is always the better buy.   {circ:True|False}

parts.label: c
parts.text: Tap A fills 5 litres a minute. Tap B fills 7 litres a minute. Together they fill 12 litres a minute.   {circ:True|False}

items.explanation: (a) True: double the cans, double the cost. (b) False: the larger pack can cost more for each item. (c) True: 5 + 7 = 12.

items.text: Ali has $60 and saves $5 each week. Ben has $20 and saves $10 each week. After how many weeks do they have the same amount of money? {b}
items.explanation: At first Ali has $40 more. Each week the gap closes by $5: 8 weeks (both have $100).

items.text: A pipe delivers 1.5 litres of water every 20 seconds. How many litres does it deliver in 5 minutes? {b} litres
items.explanation: 5 minutes is 300 seconds, which is 15 lots of 20 seconds. 15 × 1.5 = 22.5 litres.

items.text: Pen packs: A has 5 pens for $3.00, B has 8 pens for $4.70 and C has 12 pens for $6.90. Mei needs exactly 32 pens and may mix packs. Find the least total cost. $ {bw}
items.hint: List every way to make 32 pens with whole packs.
items.explanation: Ways to make 32 pens: B + 2C = $18.50; 4B = $18.80; 4A + C = $18.90. The least is $18.50.

items.text: Alone, hose P needs 20 minutes to fill a pool. Alone, hose Q needs 30 minutes to fill the same pool. Find the time to fill the pool when both hoses are on. {b} minutes
items.hint: Try a pool size that suits both hoses.
items.explanation: Pretend 60 litres. P: 3 a minute. Q: 2 a minute. Together 5 a minute. 60 ÷ 5 = 12 minutes.

items.text: 5 identical machines make 400 bolts in 4 minutes. How many of these machines are needed to make 900 bolts in 3 minutes? {b}
items.hint: Find the bolts for 1 machine in 1 minute first.
items.explanation: 1 machine makes 400 ÷ 5 ÷ 4 = 20 bolts a minute. 900 ÷ 3 = 300 a minute, so 15 machines.

items.text: A tank holds 120 litres. The first 60 litres go in at 6 litres a minute and the second 60 litres at 12 litres a minute. Average rate = total litres ÷ total minutes. Find the average rate for the whole tank. {b} litres a minute
items.hint: Find the minutes for each half first. Then add the minutes.
items.explanation: First half 60 ÷ 6 = 10 minutes. Second half 60 ÷ 12 = 5 minutes. 120 ÷ 15 = 8 litres a minute (not 9: more time is spent at the slow rate).

items.text: Tank A has 90 litres. A pump takes 5 litres out of it each minute. Tank B has 10 litres. A tap puts 3 litres into it each minute. After how many minutes do the 2 tanks have the same amount of water? {b} minutes
items.hint: How many litres does the gap between the tanks close each minute?
items.explanation: A has 80 litres more. The gap closes by 5 + 3 = 8 a minute: 10 minutes (40 litres each).

items.text: Tap A fills 9 litres a minute. Tap B fills 11 litres a minute. Tap A is turned on at the start. Tap B is turned on 8 minutes later. How many minutes after the start is a 312 litre tank full? {b} minutes
items.hint: What has happened before tap B is turned on?
items.explanation: Tap A alone: 8 × 9 = 72 litres. 240 left at 20 a minute: 12 minutes. 8 + 12 = 20 minutes.

items.text: A copier makes 54 copies in 3 minutes. How many in 8 minutes? {b}
items.explanation: 54 ÷ 3 = 18 copies in 1 minute. 8 × 18 = 144 copies.

items.text: 5 mangoes cost $4.00. 8 mangoes cost $6.00.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The better buy is   {circ:5 mangoes|8 mangoes}

items.explanation: 5 mangoes: $4.00 ÷ 5 = $0.80 each. 8 mangoes: $6.00 ÷ 8 = $0.75 each. $0.75 is less, so 8 mangoes is the better buy.

items.text: Tap A fills 9 litres a minute, tap B fills 11 and a leak loses 4. All 3 work together. Find the time to fill 160 litres. {b} min
items.explanation: The tank gains 9 + 11 - 4 = 16 litres each minute. 160 ÷ 16 = 10 minutes.

items.text: Bike hire costs $5.00 for the first 30 minutes. After that it costs $2.00 for each 20 minutes, and a part of 20 minutes counts as a whole one. How much for 1 hour 55 minutes? $ {b}
items.explanation: First 30 minutes $5.00. 85 minutes is 5 lots of 20: 5 × $2.00 = $10.00. Total $15.00.
